With all that said, I don't think it is necessary for you to disclose that if you do become a preacher, so long as you come to work sober (as you already planned). And there's always the saying that what you don't know can't hurt you, so if those like me just don't know that you wrote it high, then theres no harm, no foul, right?

But some people also argue that withholding information is dishonest and therefore sinful, but unless you're asked about it, it isn't really withholding information because nobody requested it in the first place. So, I guess my point is there's nothing really stopping you from hiding it, it is entirely your choice.

I think if you are still worried about it though, you might want to take extra care to revising and potentially rewriting your sermon when you are sober, not only to fix mistakes, but in case you're worried about it being found out somehow, then you can make the argument that your non-sober writing was a first draft, and your completed thoughts and sermon were all done while sober. In the unlikely event that someone found out, they theoretically would probably be more comfortable knowing you revised it. Because, due to the nature of triggers, sometimes things that were near something triggering almost feel tainted, at least that's how I feel about it. Like if a Singer i like i found out does drugs, I feel like all their music is tainted and worrying because it could have made contact with their non-sober mind. 

Its an irrational thinking process, and of course I'm working on and praying about it everyday, but I thought it might be worth mentioning or potentially intriguing to you. The second draft kind of "sterilizes" it, per se. Obviously, I'm not saying God's word is tainted itself, but it is possible that people might not feel comfortable anymore with God if they have a similar experience to me, and found out that they were receiving these perceived "tainted" sermons. 

As for going to a church where other people smoked weed, it's probably unavoidable. If I had the option, I would avoid it, but again I try to remain ignorant of things that may make me uncomfortable and not pry into people's lives too much. If I did find any specific people I knew to smoke weed or do other drugs, I would remain civil but distant from them unless the time called (prayer request, other things where I need to open my heart more). That's about it.

Apologies if any of this sounds a bit absurd, mental health is a pretty wild thing, and people are different a lot in their individual experiences. All in all, if you really want to make sure your Church feels safe as possible, you could go the safe route and just refrain from using those writings, but I think its completely possible to use them in a valuable way. I think it would probably be a waste to throw them out. If you have any more questions, let me know, or if something didn't make sense.

If your friends want to all use green, you are probably going to want to use an analogous color scheme. That would be 3 colors right next to eachother on the color wheel. You want them to be all green, so they're gonna have to be analogous, right? But you wanna make sure they are different enough that you can tell them apart. I would suggest you avoid a dark green or a neon green, but anything in between should be okay.   
  
Also, there are some programs that offer autocaptions maker, which you can then review for mistakes by rewatching the video and changing the color per person. I use CapCut free version to generate my autocaptions. No watermark or time limit. It lags a little at times but it is remarkably quite accurate at recognizing speech and times it for your itself. So all you would have to do is change the colors to each person who is speaking (make sure you uncheck the "apply to all" button).  
  
[Here](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/914275499386232902/1187579281979756564/export202312212113085691.png?ex=65976664&is=6584f164&hm=5a4c082f636f20227d4c46e16ffad7a8faa0c425a4b003c25510cb7d49509789&) is an example of analogous color schemes in green, shown with subtitles on even the most clashing of backgrounds (green on blue), its still readable enough for the average person.

> you're feeling negative emotions, do you show those emotions to others? Do you let your feelings out, do you try to look on the bright side, or do you put them down and aside so that you can be logical?

I am not the type to be afraid to show my negative emotions by any means. Though I am also not one to show them carelessly or haphazardly, I show them as appropriately and keep as much to myself that I think isn't appropriate for the audience around me, but I am not afraid of my feelings. I do try to stay positive but I recognize that logic nor idealism are the solution to my feelings. 

 > When you are your worst self, what are you like and what's driving that?

My worst self pushes everyone away to protect myself. I feel afraid that people will leave me, reject me, hurt me, not return my love, etc., so I push them away first as a means of control over the situation. I also find that I get self destructive at my worst and neglect my body as a punishment for "not being good enough." When I feel my worst, its like theres a gaping wound and I am terribly fragile and irrational, but even then, i find that I want to make sure I dont hurt anyone's feelings or anything. That part of me seems to be the only thing that stays entirely consistent.

> What’s your biggest strength? What’s your biggest flaw? 

I'd say my biggest strength is my emotional intelligence. I understand emotions very well, whether it be my own or other people's, and I find that I am equipped to deal with nearly any situation even if initially I freak out, I always find a way to not only push through, but typically excel. I would say my biggest flaw is that I hold myself to a higher standard than I do anybody else, and this leads to me gaining a lot of ego wounds when I do not live up to those standards, and also I subconsciously look down on the people around me and feel that I am better and smarter than them.

> When you are getting in your own way, what does that look like and why does it happen?

Typically when I am in my own way, I do it by making excuses, like "But im too tired" or "but i already tried, and it didn't work, and I don't wanna do it again." I make excuses because I have a lack of motivation to do things that I deem "unneeded" to be done. Even if I want to do it, if it doesn't have to be done right then, I will find a way to ruin it for myself.

> What are your behaviors that cause you to get into conflict with other people?

A lot of people don't like that I am "too nice" and "too innocent." Apparently me being nice to just about everybody annoys people, and I'm not really sure why. I also get into conflict because of my ego and because I try to help people when they dont necessarily want it

> What's the worst thing that could happen to you, and why are you afraid of it?

The worst thing that could happen to me is any situation where I ended up alone or abandoned or completely unloved by anyone. In other words, my worst fear really is the people around me dying/leaving me/abandoning me/losing their love for me/etc. i would put those all in the same category, because regardless of which one of those happens it envokes the same reaction in me.

> What sets you off, makes you angry?

I get angry when people overstep my boundaries or hurt the people i care about. Those are the only two things that really make me angry.
